relations.subject: sgw:sync-gateway-instance
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted requiresDedicatedNode) - directly the predicate the coordinator flagged as relevant to this page's topology guidance
relations.evidence: In a production environment, they are expected to be deployed on separate machines. This is because the Sync Gateway is typically deployed to be internet-facing and sits in the "Application tier" whilst Couchbase Server is deployed in the "Database tier".

relations.subject: sgw:import-node
relations.evidence: An import node is a node designated to handle document import processing.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cache
relations.evidence: Tuning the channel and revision cache is an [Enterprise Edition](https://www.couchbase.com/products/editions) feature.

relations.subject: sgw:revision-cache
relations.evidence: Tuning the channel and revision cache is an [Enterprise Edition](https://www.couchbase.com/products/editions) feature.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cache
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted hasExecutionConstraint) - unbounded growth is a stated scaling limit of the instance hosting it
relations.evidence: The size of channel cache will grow unbounded with the number of channels, regardless of the number of active channels.

relations.subject: tool:sync-gateway
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted usesExecutionModel) - lightweight threads plus async I/O is the concurrency model named for the binary/instance
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway is designed for multiprocessing. It uses lightweight threads and asynchronous I/O.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.evidence: every write operation gets processed by the [Sync Function](../access-control/sync-function/sync-function.md) and triggers notifications to other clients with read access, who then perform reads to get the new data.

notable_absence.finding: Like index-partitions.json's partitioning guardrails (same batch), the constraint against running import processing on multiple nodes is stated only as prose discouragement with no enforced limit: 'it is strongly discouraged for multiple Sync Gateway nodes in the cluster to be configured for import processing' - no validation, role gate, or hard cap is described. This is the second instance in this batch of the same pattern (operator-discipline-only guardrail), suggesting it may be a recurring Sync Gateway design philosophy rather than a one-off gap.

cross_component_finding: This page cross-references three OTHER pages in this same batch by name for deeper detail on points it only summarizes: the Load Balancer guide (for coordinating multiple instances), the OS Level Tuning guide (for socket/connection management), and GSI/SQL++ indexing (for Index Service resource sizing) - deployment.md functions as this batch's topology/sizing hub, tying together load-balancer.md, os-level-tuning.md and indexing.md rather than duplicating their content.
cross_product_finding: This page's swappiness recommendation ('changing the Linux swappiness value to 0') is not explained on this page at all - it is entirely delegated via cross-reference to a Couchbase SERVER installation guide (server/current/install/install-swap-space.md), outside both this batch and the sync-gateway/ product tree. Sync Gateway deployment guidance directly imports a Couchbase Server OS-tuning doc rather than restating the swappiness rationale for its own RAM-optimized design.
